scope: What US Vinted sellers pay (nothing) and what buyers pay on top. Bumps, custom shipping and item verification are out of scope.
structure: Sellers pay nothing to list or sell: after an order completes, the full agreed item price is credited to the seller's Vinted Wallet, and withdrawals to a US bank account (USD only) are free, take up to 5 business days, and require a minimum of $0.10. The buyer pays, on top of the item price, a mandatory Vinted fee (called the Buyer Protection fee until 2026). Vinted's Price List and help center both describe it as 'usually 5% + $0.70': a percentage of the item's or bundle's price plus a fixed fee, which can vary by item characteristics, order value and order type. Optional seller-paid item bumps are priced at checkout by duration (3 or 7 calendar days), item price and local or international scope. For US–UK cross-border orders the buyer pays the same Vinted fee and a 1.2% currency conversion built into the checkout exchange rate; the seller is paid in USD.
quotes: There are no fees for uploading your items or selling them on Vinted. This means once your sale is successfully closed, you'll receive the full selling price straight to your Vinted Wallet.
The Vinted fee is a mandatory platform fee paid at checkout when you place an order through Vinted using the “Buy now” button (please see our Terms and Conditions for full information).
The fee typically includes a percentage of the item's or bundle's price, as well as a fixed fee — usually 5% + $0.70.
At checkout, the total Vinted fee, which includes any Sales Taxes, will be added to the order's final price and clearly displayed in the order summary.
The Vinted fee typically includes a percentage of the item's or bundle's price, as well as a fixed fee — usually 5% + $0.70.
The calculation of this fee varies based on several factors, such as: item characteristics order value order type (a single item versus a bundle)
The Vinted fee is a mandatory platform fee paid at checkout when you place an order through Vinted.
The duration of the Item Bump may last for 3 or 7 calendar days.

The Fee for Bumping Listed Items will vary depending on the chosen duration, item price, and the chosen territorial scope (local or international). Any applicable Sales Tax charged will be included in the price shown at a checkout.
It can take up to 5 business days for the funds to arrive in your bank account. Business days are Monday–Friday, not including weekends and public holidays.
You can withdraw earnings in dollars (USD) to supported accounts in banks or other financial institutions using account and routing numbers.
The minimum amount you can withdraw is $0.10.
When making international purchases on Vinted, the same Vinted fee applies as for domestic transactions.
Our payment provider applies a 1.2% currency conversion fee to USD↔GBP transactions, which is included in the conversion rate provided at the checkout.
Item Verification is currently available in France, Italy, Belgium, Germany, Spain, The Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Denmark, Sweden, Lithuania and Finland.
The service fee is paid for by buyers and is visible on the item page and the checkout.

notes: The Price List (last updated 10/08/2026) and help article 342 now agree: the fee is 'usually 5% + $0.70' and its calculation 'varies based on several factors'. Until that update the Price List gave an exact formula ($0.70 + 5% of the item price) under the name Buyer Protection Fee. The calculator shows 5% + $0.70 as the usual case; the amount at checkout can differ.

Seller-side charges: none found on US pages beyond optional bumps. No instant-withdrawal option or fee is documented for the US (the Wallet page says funds become available 2 days after order completion; bank withdrawal takes up to 5 business days).

'Offline verification': Vinted's Item Verification for designer items is buyer-paid and, per the loaded page, not available in the US. 'Electronics Verification' appears only in search-engine snippets — UNVERIFIED.
The Price List and help pages were served for the US locale (English, US; USD amounts); the same URL serves other countries' formulas under other locales.
Failed pages: /help/432 (Withdrawals) redirected to the Help Centre home; the /help/4/1577 'Payments & withdrawals' topic index did not render server-side.

Vinted is not a fee-on-seller marketplace, so a seller-fee calculator should return fee = 0 and net = item price; the Vinted fee is relevant only for showing the buyer's total (item + usually 5% + $0.70, plus shipping and tax).

Re-read 2026-10-12. Vinted rewrote the Price List on 10/08/2026. The fee is now called the Vinted fee throughout, and the Price List no longer gives a fixed formula: it says the fee 'typically includes a percentage of the item's or bundle's price, as well as a fixed fee — usually 5% + $0.70'. The sentences about who pays shipping and the taxes on shipping labels are gone from the page, as is the bundle wording, so this schedule no longer states them. Sellers still pay nothing; the numbers in this schedule are unchanged.

Re-read 2026-10-21. Vinted reworded its 'How to withdraw earnings' article: bank withdrawals 'can take up to 5 business days for the funds to arrive in your bank account. Business days are Monday–Friday, not including weekends and public holidays', and the minimum reads 'The minimum amount you can withdraw is $0.10.', with the sentence 'Withdrawals below this amount will fail.' gone from every readable page. The figures, up to 5 business days and a $0.10 minimum, and every rate are unchanged, and the calculator uses none of these sentences.
summary: Vinted charges US sellers nothing to list, sell or withdraw: you receive the full item price. The buyer pays a Vinted fee on top, which Vinted says is usually 5% of the item price plus $0.70 but can vary.

examples.description: Arithmetic check derived from the published Price List: a $25 item — the seller receives $25; the buyer usually pays 5% + $0.70 ($1.95) on top.
